reason: This text is the Song of the Sea (Exodus 15) in which the Israelites celebrate Yahweh's deliverance from Egypt with praise and worship. The song depicts God's righteous anger directed exclusively at Egypt and Pharaoh for their oppression ('You send your wrath, it consumes them like stubble'), not at the Israelites. The text shows the people actively and properly worshiping Yahweh through song and praise ('I will sing to Yahweh...'), and they are being blessed and led to their promised sanctuary as a result. There is no indication of anger toward the people for improper worship; rather, the text demonstrates the opposite pattern—proper worship met with divine favor and deliverance.
